arxiv-2110-05388.title: Quantitative Equality in Substructural Logic via Lipschitz doctrines
arxiv-2110-05388.creator: Francesco Dagnino ORCID:0000-0003-3599-3535, Fabio Pasquali ORCID:0000-0002-3599-5525
arxiv-2110-05388.description: Abstract . Substructural logics naturally support a quantitative interpretation of formulas, as they are seen as consumable resources. Distances are the quantitative counterpart of equivalence relations: they measure how much two objects are similar, rather than just saying whether they are equivalent or not. Hence, they provide the natural choice for modelling equality in a substructural setting.

arxiv-2112-05517.title: N N -sociable Heronian triangles
arxiv-2112-05517.creator: Nart Shalqini
arxiv-2112-05517.description: Abstract A Heronian triangle is a triangle that has integer side lengths and integer area. Praton and Shalqini [ 1 ] define amicable Heronian triangles to be two Heronian triangles where the area of one equals the perimeter of the other, and vice versa; analogous to the concept of amicable numbers.

arxiv-2206-13855.title: Arithmetically equivalent number fields have approximately the same successive minima
arxiv-2206-13855.creator: Floris Vermeulen
arxiv-2206-13855.description: Abstract . Let K K and K ′ K^{\prime} be arithmetically equivalent number fields, both of degree d d . We prove that K K and K ′ K^{\prime} have the same successive minima, up to a constant depending only on d d . We give examples showing that one cannot expect equality. 1.

arxiv-2208-10162.title: Unscented Kalman filter with stable embedding for simple, accurate and computationally efficient state estimation of systems on manifolds in Euclidean space Publication type: Article Type
arxiv-2208-10162.creator: Jae-Hyeon Park, Dong Eui Chang*, J. Park, D. E. Chang
arxiv-2208-10162.description: Abstract This paper proposes a simple, accurate and computationally efficient method to apply the ordinary unscented Kalman filter developed in Euclidean space to systems whose dynamics evolve on manifolds. We use the mathematical theory called stable embedding to make a variant of unscented Kalman filter that keeps state estimates in close proximity to the manifold while exhibiting excellent estimation performance.

arxiv-2301-04462.title: An Analysis of Quantile Temporal-Difference Learning
arxiv-2301-04462.creator: Mark Rowland markrowland@google.com, Rémi Munos, Mohammad Gheshlaghi Azar, Yunhao Tang, Georg Ostrovski, Anna Harutyunyan, Karl Tuyls, Marc G. Bellemare, Will Dabney
arxiv-2301-04462.description: Abstract We analyse quantile temporal-difference learning (QTD), a distributional reinforcement learning algorithm that has proven to be a key component in several successful large-scale applications of reinforcement learning. Despite these empirical successes, a theoretical understanding of QTD has proven elusive until now.

arxiv-2307-11620.title: Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Global-to-Local Value Regularization
arxiv-2307-11620.creator: Xiangsen Wang, Haoran Xu, Yinan Zheng, Xianyuan Zhan
arxiv-2307-11620.description: Abstract Offline reinforcement learning (RL) has received considerable attention in recent years due to its attractive capability of learning policies from offline datasets without environmental interactions. Despite some success in the single-agent setting, offline multi-agent RL (MARL) remains to be a challenge. The large joint state-action space and the coupled multi-agent behaviors pose extra complexities for offline policy optimization.

arxiv-2308-15678.title: Understanding step selection analysis through numerical integration
arxiv-2308-15678.creator: Théo Michelot 1 , Natasha J. Klappstein 1 , Jonathan R. Potts 2 , John Fieberg 3
arxiv-2308-15678.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Théo Michelot 1 , Natasha J. Klappstein 1 , Jonathan R. Potts 2 , John Fieberg 3. Step selection functions (SSFs) are flexible statistical models used to jointly describe animals’ movement and habitat preferences.

arxiv-2506-19344.title: Image Segmentation using Chan-Vese Active Contours
arxiv-2506-19344.creator: Pranav Shenoy K. P
arxiv-2506-19344.description: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive derivation and implementation of the Chan–Vese active contour model for image segmentation. The model, derived from the Mumford–Shah variational framework, evolves contours based on regional intensity differences rather than image gradients, making it highly effective for segmenting noisy images or images with weak boundaries.

arxiv-2509-25638.title: Generalized Contrastive Learning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval
arxiv-2509-25638.creator: Jungsoo Lee Janghoon Cho Hyojin Park Munawar Hayat, Kyuwoong Hwang Fatih Porikli Sungha Choi, Qualcomm AI Research {jungsool, janghoon, hyojinp, hayat, kyuwoong, fporikli, sunghac}@qti.qualcomm.com
arxiv-2509-25638.description: Abstract Despite their consistent performance improvements, cross-modal retrieval models ( e.g. , CLIP) show degraded performances with retrieving keys composed of fused image-text modality ( e.g., Wikipedia pages with both images and text). To address this critical challenge, multimodal retrieval has been recently explored to develop a unified single retrieval model capable of retrieving keys across diverse modality combinations.

britannica-1911-model-yachting.title: Model-Yachting (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-model-yachting.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-model-yachting.description: Article 'Model-Yachting' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. It has always been customary for ship-builders to make a miniature model of the vessel under construction, which is in every respect a copy of the original on a small scale, whether steam-ship or sailing-vessel (there is a fine collection in the Victoria and Albert Museum, London). Many of these models are of exquisite workmanship, every rope, pulley or portion of the engine being faithfully reproduced.

pmc-10497569.title: Intravenous immunoglobulins improve skin fibrosis in experimental models of systemic sclerosis
pmc-10497569.creator: Silvia Speca, Meryem-Maud Farhat, Manel Jendoubi, Thomas Guerrier, Sébastien Sanges, Delphine Staumont-Sallé, Eric Hachulla, Sylvain Dubucquoi, Vincent Sobanski, Aurore Collet, David Launay
pmc-10497569.description: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is the most severe systemic autoimmune disease with currently no cure. Intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIg) are an attractive candidate in this disease to counteract inflammation and fibrosis but data are scarce and conflicting. This study, assessed the effects of IVIg in a murine HOCl-induced model of SSc.

pmc-10504908.title: Deciphering the Mechanism of Xijiao Dihuang Decoction in Treating Psoriasis by Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation
pmc-10504908.creator: Yicheng Guo, Huiqun Gan, Shigui Xu, Guosheng Zeng, Lili Xiao, Zhijun Ding, Jie Zhu, Xinglong Xiong, Zhiyuan Fu
pmc-10504908.description: PurposeThis study aims to confirm the efficacy of Xijiao Dihuang decoction (XJDHT), a classic prescription, in treating psoriasis and to explore the potential therapeutic mechanism.MethodsFor pharmacodynamic analysis, a mouse model of imiquimod cream (IMQ)-induced psoriasis was constructed. Active ingredients and genes of XJDHT, as well as psoriasis-related targets, were obtained from public databases.

pmc-10575548.title: The Synchrony-Prosociality Link Cannot Be Explained Away as Expectancy Effect: Response to Atwood et al. (2022)
pmc-10575548.creator: Bahar Tunçgenç, Joshua S Bamford, Christine Fawcett, Emma Cohen
pmc-10575548.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Moving in time to others, as is often observed in dance, music, sports and much of children’s play cross-culturally, is thought to make people feel and act more prosocially towards each other. In a recent paper, Atwood et al. (2022) argued that the inferential validity of this link found between synchronous behaviour and prosociality might be mainly due to “expectancy effects generated by a combination of (1) experimenter expectancy, leading to experimenter bias; and (2) participant expectancy (i.e., placebo effects)”.

pmc-10628213.title: X-ray reflectivity study of the heat shock protein Hsp70 interaction with an artificial cell membrane model
pmc-10628213.creator: Ali Makky, Julian Czajor, Oleg Konovalov, Alexander Zhakhov, Alexander Ischenko, Ankita Behl, Shailja Singh, Wasim Abuillan, Maxim Shevtsov
pmc-10628213.description: Membrane-bound heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70) apart from its intracellular localization was shown to be specifically expressed on the plasma membrane surface of tumor but not normal cells. Although the association of Hsp70 with lipid membranes is well documented the exact mechanisms for chaperone membrane anchoring have not been fully elucidated.

pmc-10641331.title: Soluble Fiber Effect on Human Serum Leptin and Adiponectin: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis
pmc-10641331.creator: Ali Zeinabi, Hadi Ghaedi, Seyed Ali Hosseini
pmc-10641331.description: Literature showed that soluble fiber has beneficial effects on cardiometabolic risk factors and leptin and adiponectin serum levels. Our aim in this meta-analysis was to determine the effect of soluble fiber supplementation on leptin and adiponectin serum levels. A systematic search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and ISI Web of Science for eligible trials up to December 2021.

pmc-11435735.title: Optimizing Real-Time MI-BCI Performance in Post-Stroke Patients: Impact of Time Window Duration on Classification Accuracy and Responsiveness
pmc-11435735.creator: Aleksandar Miladinović, Agostino Accardo, Joanna Jarmolowska, Uros Marusic, Miloš Ajčević
pmc-11435735.description: Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) are promising tools for motor neurorehabilitation. Achieving a balance between classification accuracy and system responsiveness is crucial for real-time applications. This study aimed to assess how the duration of time windows affects performance, specifically classification accuracy and the false positive rate, to optimize the temporal parameters of MI-BCI systems.

pmc-11549559.title: Arginine impacts aggregation, biofilm formation, and antibiotic susceptibility in Enterococcus faecalis
pmc-11549559.creator: Alex P Snell, Dawn A Manias, Reham R Elbehery, Gary M Dunny, Julia L E Willett
pmc-11549559.description: Enterococcus faecalis is a commensal bacterium in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract of humans and other organisms. E. faecalis also causes infections in root canals, wounds, the urinary tract, and on heart valves. E. faecalis metabolizes arginine through the arginine deiminase pathway, which converts arginine to ornithine and releases ATP, ammonia, and CO2. E.

pmc-11682847.title: Assessing ChatGPT’s Reliability as an Educational Resource for Information on Breast Reduction Surgery
pmc-11682847.creator: Emanuella M Brito, Isabel C Bernal, Andres A Mascaro-Pankova, James W Fletcher, Eric S Weiss, Christopher J Low, Michael C Cheung, Martin I Newman
pmc-11682847.description: Introduction: With advances in AI and machine learning, platforms like OpenAI’s ChatGPT are emerging as educational resources. While these platforms offer easy access and user-friendliness due to their personalized conversational responses, concerns about the accuracy and reliability of their information persist.

pmc-12542801.title: Hybrid diacrylate resin-gelatin methacryloyl composite with bone-to-brain stiffness range
pmc-12542801.creator: Mohammad Naghavi Zadeh, Kapil D. Patel, Daniel Gosden, James A. Smith, Paul J. Gates, Qiukai Qi, Fabrizio Scarpa, Andrew Conn, Adam W. Perriman, Jonathan Rossiter
pmc-12542801.description: Biointerfacing techniques for connecting implants to living tissues are advancing, but matching stiffness at hard-soft interfaces, such as between tendon and bone, remains challenging. This is critical for improving biomechanical tissue models, repairing trauma, and integrating soft robotic technologies like artificial muscles.

pmc-12613653.title: Spatiotemporal trajectory of life expectancy and its disparity in China 2000–2030: modelling and prediction
pmc-12613653.creator: Yuqing Feng, Jinfeng Wang, Naliang Guo, Yue Cai, Qian Yin, Shiyong Wu
pmc-12613653.description: BackgroundLife expectancy (LE) is one of crucial metrics of human evolution. However, the evolutionary trajectories of LE in different regions of China and the regional inequalities expected in 2030 are still unclear yet.MethodsThis study collected provincial LE data and relevant explanatory variables for the years of 2000, 2010, 2020 in China.

pmc-13096697.title: Evaluation of antigen and antibody assays for surveillance of Lassa virus in peri-domestic rodents in southeastern Sierra Leone: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13096697.creator: Allison R Smither, James Koninga, Franklyn B Kanneh, Momoh Foday, Matthew L Boisen, Nell G Bond, Mambu Momoh, John D Sandi, Lansana Kanneh, Foday Alhasan, Ibrahim M Kanneh, Mohamed S Yillah, Donald S Grant, Duane J Bush, Diana K S Nelson, Kaitlin M Cruz, Raphaëlle Klitting, Matthias G Pauthner, Kris
pmc-13096697.description: SummaryBackgroundLassa fever, caused by Lassa mammarenavirus (LASV), is a rodent-borne disease endemic to west Africa. Zoonotic surveillance of LASV provides epidemiological insights into its potential presence. We aimed to assess LASV antigen and antibody prevalence in peri-domestic rodents in southeastern Sierra Leone.

pmc-13103560.title: Pathways from physical exercise to life satisfaction among Chinese university students: The chain mediating role of exercise adherence and health literacy
pmc-13103560.creator: Zhong-lei Cui, Wen-hao Zhang, Wei Wang, Shan-shan Han, Sai Zhu, Chuan-yi Xu, Hua-sheng Huang, Rong-hai Luo
pmc-13103560.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the influence of physical exercise on life satisfaction among college students. To further explore the underlying mechanisms, two mediating variables were introduced: exercise adherence and health literacy. This approach helped analyze the pathway through which physical exercise predicts and affects students’ life satisfaction.

pmc-13207936.title: Hesperidin Mitigates Bisphenol-A Induced Oxidative Stress, Endocrine Disruption and Testicular Damage in Adult Male Wistar Rats
pmc-13207936.creator: Augustine Oviosun, Ezinne Chidinma Oviosun, Ibe Micheal Usman, Chinyere Nkemjika Anyanwu, Vivian Onyinye Ojiakor, Emmanuel Anayochukwu Esom, Emeka Godson Anyanwu
pmc-13207936.description: IntroductionBisphenol A (BPA), a well-known endocrine disruptor, is newly emerging as causing male infertility by endocrine disturbances, induction of oxidative stress and testicular toxicity. This study investigates the protective role of hesperidin against BPA-induced testicular toxicity in male Wistar rats.
